usage: Used when moving a plant into a new pot with fresh soil; this is the natural everyday term for repotting.
Often collocates with plants, seedlings, orchids, and houseplants. You can say it when talking about care, maintenance, or giving a plant more space.
It is an action word, so it usually appears in a sentence as a verb phrase rather than a standalone noun in casual speech.
Common in home gardening and plant shops; in more technical writing, people may also use the English loanword 'repot' or more formal gardening terms.
